The brutal selloff in Kioxia Holdings Corp. on worries over the AI boom’s sustainability has made it the cheapest Japanese blue chip, reinforcing bullish analyst calls.
The Japanese storage chipmaker’s stock has plunged more than 40% this month to trade at around 1.7 times forward earnings estimates. Its valuation has fallen below that of Tokyo Electric Power Co., to the bottom of the Nikkei 225. It’s also now the cheapest on a measure of memory peers, below SK Hynix Inc.

Save
Australia adopted a law requiring liquefied natural gas exporters to reserve as much as a fifth of their supply for the domestic market.
Legislation introduced by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese’s Labor government requiring major LNG exporters including Shell Plc, ConocoPhillips, Woodside Energy Ltd. and TotalEnergies SE to ensure more gas is available for Australian consumers passed the House of Representatives early on Friday. The obligation will kick in Jan. 1, 2028.

Asian stocks may look to build on a tech rally that powered gains in US stock futures on Thursday, with signs of a revival in risk appetite lifting assets including copper and Bitcoin. Oil climbed after Yemen’s Houthi rebels struck a key Saudi Refinery.
Equity-index futures for Japan, South Korea and Australia pointed to modest gains. Contracts for S&P 500 Index and the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.5% each on Thursday, while Europe’s Stoxx 600 rallied 1.7%. US cash markets were shut for the Thanksgiving holiday.

Save
Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Deteriorating conditions in financial markets are preventing a new Canadian issuer from selling debt as planned, even with the backing of one of the country’s most important pension managers.
CDP Infrastructures Group Inc., the issuing entity for La Caisse’s infrastructure financing platform, paused an inaugural debt sale of as much as C$1 billion ($702 million), according to people familiar with the matter. Strains in credit markets meant the firm would have been forced to sell the bonds at wider spreads and possibly reduce the deal size, said the people, speaking on condition they not be identified because they aren’t authorized to speak publicly.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Ghana redeemed a four-year domestic bond three months ahead of maturity, as the government sought to bolster investor confidence in an economy recovering from a debt restructuring.
The West African nation bought back all the 12.6 billion cedis ($1.1 billion), or 44% of the outstanding securities, which were tendered by investors at the end of a three-day offer, the Finance Ministry said in a statement. The government also paid 289 million cedis in interest that accrued, it said.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Copper recovered from an 11-month low on Thursday alongside gains in other commodities and technology stocks, as investors returned to riskier assets following days of sharp losses.
Three-month copper futures on the London Metal Exchange rose to settle 1.9% higher, trimming this month’s steep losses, which were driven by worries about the artificial intelligence trade and looming US interest-rate hikes. All six base metals on the LME saw prices gain Thursday, a public holiday in the US.

item.title: New Zealand Poised to Learn Who Can Form Its Next Government
item.description: New Zealand will learn Friday who is in a position to form its next government, three weeks after an election that was too close to call.

item.title: KKR Banks Line Up €550 Million of Debt to Back Logoplaste Buyout
item.description: Banks have lined up €550 million ($603.5 million) of loans to back KKR & Co.’s acquisition of packaging company Logoplaste, according to people familiar with the situation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Encouraged Local Banks to Finance Deal for Gold Miner
item.description: Kazakhstan has encouraged domestic banks to lend more than $1 billion to construction tycoon Shakhmurat Mutalip and revised financing regulations to help him buy gold miner AK Altynalmas JSC, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Altria, Japan Tobacco Explore Takeover of Imperial Brands
item.description: Altria Group Inc. and Japan Tobacco Inc. are exploring a potential takeover of British cigarette maker Imperial Brands Plc, accelerating consolidation in the declining cigarette market in what would be one of the biggest UK acquisitions in a decade.

item.title: Gold Hovers Near 15-Month Low as Traders Eye Fed Path, AI Stocks
item.description: Gold hovered near the lowest level in about 15 months on Thursday, as investors weighed the prospect of further Federal Reserve rate hikes against a relief rally in wider markets amid a comeback in technology shares.
